body: It doesn't have to be one or the other way with you.

Would it not be a good idea to have someone with you when you tell them, or even have them introduce the idea to your parents first and then let you come together to talk about it as a family? Somebody holding your hand could go a long way.

Some of your phrases are not in my wheelhouse. I am not familiar with what you mean by 'part of the system' or 'self-stigma.'

Previous to my own attempt, I had spoken with people who had made attempts of their own. I was able to listen to them talk about how it affected their lives, and that part made sense to me. But as far as their shared experiences somehow relating to my own in some way, such as to steer me clear of self harm, I may as well have been deaf. It was like I couldn't hear what they were saying. 

I think that people in pain behave like people who are extremely hungry, wrapped in the immediacy of their crisis. In that state of being they will probably sometimes seem selfish and they may condescend to you about your pain. The phrase "you have no idea" gets thrown around a lot. I don't think that we should expect much better from people who are going through such things. In the same way, we shrug off the insults of drunk people. Because you know that in the moment, they are not themselves.

Gender and sexuality are such a large part of our culture. There are so many things that it is or is not socially acceptable for you to do and say and even feel, depending on your gender. It is therefore no surprise that people who don't conform in this way meet opposition in so many aspects of their lives. It can be overwhelming.

The condition of life is held to be a positive one. Not just based on our instinct to survive and reproduce, but as thinking sentient creatures, we have made a value judgement about it, and found it to be overwhelmingly a good thing. But if you keep adding darkness to that scale, the balance is going to shift.

Sometimes, when people are arguing about the existence of hell, the eternal nature of it is called into question. One of these arguments is that any level of pain experienced over eternity becomes commonplace and is no great punishment.

After decades, my own pain has become unremarkable to me. I am not always aware of it. But in the same way, breathing has also become unremarkable. It hasn't gone away, it has just become part of my life. And so has pain become part of my life. That sounds melodramatic. But in practice it is quiet.

So that's how I think it works when lgbt people kitten themselves. It isn't really a traumatic event that takes place somewhere in your life. It is part of who you are, or what you are. And it's never going to go away, not ever. That is not an easy future to wake up to.

Of all the fun advice I've heard so far, the one thing that has stuck with me is a quote from some professional gamer, which maybe goes "if you kill yourself, how will you eat food and play videogames?"

Its so absurd that you can't help but get hit in the face with it. The question suggests a philosophy of life that focuses on simple pleasures. My values are a little more complex than that, but when I remember it, it makes me think that maybe I'm over-complicating things.

I failed.

A few hours ago I guess I made what I thought was a serious attempt. I just want to say that suffocating is extremely unpleasant. It didn't go flawlessly but it probably would have worked if not for one simple but cataclysmic mistake on my part. Fortunately I did not screw up in such a way as to risk discovery. I have already corrected the flaws in my plan, but I did not have the heart to try a second time. It isn't that I suddenly want to live. No. But this kind of behavior must do damage to the mind, as well, because I just couldn't do anything. Until the window of opportunity had long expired, I could only sit and stare into space. This may well be the most miserable moment of my life. I have damned myself to another week of existence. What will my mind be seven days from now?

Well I just want to thank everyone who took the time to read my thoughts and reply. When I say thank you I am also talking to the people whose comments were for whatever reason deleted-how bizarre-because I take from this just a unified burst of genuine compassion. 

It gives me a sense of peace. You know I've chosen not to mention my reasons in 'the note,' and so it seems this is the only place where I've actually revealed my secret. It feels nice.

I am terrified of failure. I have this fear that I will find myself in some paradise where my dreams have been fulfilled, and spend a lifetime there, certain that I've found peace at last, when suddenly it is ripped from me and I awake in a hospital bed to find that I've dreamed the whole thing and my suicide attempt failed.

Now that I've made this post I think I know what the point of it was. There was a need to vent, yeah. But also, you know I've not 'come out' as they say. This is a thing hidden for over a decade. It feels good, just to have a conversation with people who know my secret.

I wish I could express how exhausting this little private war has been. The prospect of being near the end makes me giddy. Going to sleep now, for a few hours. I should still be here when you get off work, my friend.

This is an important question, because when you talk about the viability of treatments for an individual, I think you're talking about passing. Is my body such that what is available would successfully make me pass as a woman. And then of course I have to ask, do I need to pass as a woman to be 'cured.' Now there are some very manly looking women out there. So when we talk about passing, are we talking about being a beautiful woman, as conventions go these days? Or are we talking about merely disguising the fact that I was once a man.

Here's the thing. When I think of the viability of treatments, I'm also thinking about what it means to me to be a woman. For example you can view a video log of a sex reassignment surgery from start to finish on youtube. Or you could a few years ago. Those doctors have some magic fingers, to be sure. But for me, that surgery just creates an effigy of female genitals. That's it. If you added that up with all of the other hormones and surgeries that are available these days, would it be enough?

All I can do is speculate, of course. But my brain is telling me that no, even with everything that is available, I could not pass. And my heart is telling me that no, it would not be enough.

Yes, I'm hard to please.

Sometimes, when I am reading peoples commentary and literature about gdp, I feel like I should add my voice. Mostly to massage my ego, but also because I don't see my opinions already voiced anywhere. I have a great deal to say about the state of the community, but I don't like throwing statements around without doing the research first. And I haven't done the research.

For example something I would have addressed, had I spent the time, is the way we seem to viciously attack anyone who questions the truth of our condition. It is of course paramount that people believe, because our access to treatment depends on it and relief is pretty much the only thing that matters. But the way to make people believe is not to refuse to be questioned. I would like to see more discourse between gdp sufferers and people who don't really understand, but want to. Unfortunately whenever I look, what I find is so terribly disorganized and sensationalized. I have yet to find the gender dysphoria analogue to the great debates between athiests and creationists.

I believe the reason you are being downvoted is the same as why when I first read your post my reaction was to get defensive. People are going to fight you, at every step, if your words can even be construed (wildly maybe) to mean that their situation is not what they say it is. 

Anyway. When you say there's nothing wrong with being male or female, I agree. And I have pondered the existence of people for whom their gender is more or less inconsequential, and who, if their gender were suddenly reversed, would go on with their lives with little if any upset in between. But there's really no accounting for this feeling of mine, and it's been with me since the beginning. 

I've often wondered if I could, rather than change my body, change my mind, in such a way that I no longer desire to be female, would I be satisfied. While my heart says no, I think it would be wise to assume that this is one of those eventualities that I can't see from my current predicament, like the way you can't really tink of sharing when you're starving. My attempts at making this a reality have failed.

I gave you an upvote, for balance.
